Enterprise Release System Manager
jobs.location:
Position Summary

The Enterprise Systems Release Manager oversees release governance, environment coordination, deployment readiness, and cross-functional planning across enterprise business and clinical systems. Initially supporting Epic and Workday, this role establishes release processes, coordinates vendor and internal activities, facilitates testing, and ensures changes are introduced with minimal operational risk.

This role manages release governance across enterprise SaaS platforms. The ideal candidate is a technically oriented project or program manager with enterprise release management experience, preferably in healthcare IT and direct exposure to Epic or other EHR platforms. They bring strong vendor management, cross-functional coordination, and stakeholder communication skills, translating technical needs into actionable plans and engaging effectively with technical teams and senior leadership. Workday, ITIL, and change management experience are preferred. This strategic role emphasizes coordination, governance, and process development over hands-on configuration or engineering.


Key responsibilities
Release Governance & Planning
Own the enterprise application release calendar for assigned platforms.
Establish and maintain release governance processes, standards, and procedures.
Develop release plans and schedules using approved templates and methodologies.
Coordinate release dependencies across application, vendor, infrastructure, and business teams.
Lead release readiness reviews and facilitate go/no-go decision meetings.
Maintain release documentation, risk assessments, and deployment records.
   
Environment & Tenant Coordination
Govern the use and lifecycle of production and non production environments across assigned platforms including standards, usage policies, refresh schedules, and access controls.
Coordinate environment refreshes, upgrades, maintenance windows, and release activities with vendors and internal stakeholders.
Ensure environments are aligned to testing, deployment, and operational requirements.
Maintain visibility into environment readiness, utilization, and release schedules.
      
Testing Governance
Partner with testing coordinators, application teams, and testing resources to plan and coordinate testing activities.
Facilitate unit, integration, regression, and user acceptance testing activities performed by application teams.
Track testing progress, risks, defects, and remediation activities.
Validate completion of release readiness criteria prior to deployment.
     
Vendor & Stakeholder Management
Serve as the primary point of coordination for release related activities involving vendors and internal teams.

jobs.title: Genomic Scientist- Pipeline Development
jobs.location:
Position Summary
Research Informatics supports basic, translational, and clinical pediatric research by delivering cutting-edge digital tools, high-performance computing (HPC), and advanced data science expertise. We bring together PhD-level bioinformaticians, genomic scientists, software engineers, and HPC specialists to collaborate with physician-scientists on work ranging from CryoEM to translational genomics.
 
As a Genomic Data Scientist, you will drive pipeline engineering and high-dimensional multi-omics analysis across pediatric rare disease initiatives. Working under general scientific direction, you will serve as a key technical and analytical contributor to genomics projects, architecting automated, reproducible workflow systems (e.g., Nextflow, WDL, Snakemake) to process and interpret RNA-seq, methylation, long-read, and whole genome/exome (WGS/WES) data.

Key Responsibilities

  • Pipeline Engineering & Workflow Automation: Design, build, optimize, and maintain scalable, reproducible bioinformatics pipelines and automated variant interpretation workflows for research and clinical-grade multi-omics data.
  • Hypothesis-Driven Data Analysis: Deploy automated analytical workflows to execute rigorous exploratory and inferential data processing on high-dimensional genomic datasets using advanced statistics, machine learning, and quantitative modeling.
  • HPC & Infrastructure Optimization: Containerize computational tools (Docker/Singularity), implement version control (Git), and optimize code performance for efficient execution across High-Performance Computing (HPC) clusters.
  • Biological Discovery & Project Execution: Partner with physician-scientists to translate raw multi-omics data into biological insights, managing computational project milestones and troubleshooting pipeline bottlenecks with minimal supervision.
  • Documentation & Scientific Communication: Thoroughly document computational pipelines and code bases, contribute to peer-reviewed scientific publications, and present analytical methods at internal and external research forums.

Minimum Qualifications
Education:

  • Bachelor's degree; PhD in Genetics, Genomics, Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, or a related quantitative field highly preferred. 

Experience:

  • A minimum of one year of position-specific experience might potentially include experience acquired through MSc or Ph.D. studies. 
  • Demonstrated experience building, maintaining, and automating bioinformatics pipelines using workflow orchestration engines (e.g., Nextflow, WDL, Snakemake).
  • Strong programming proficiency in Python, R, and Bash in Linux/Unix High-Performance Computing (HPC) environments, including experience with containerization (Docker/Singularity) and version control (Git).
  • Computational experience analyzing multi-omic datasets (WGS/WES, RNA sequencing, methylation, or long-read platforms).
  • Experience with human genetics research, variant annotation tools, and familiarity with clinical NGS testing frameworks or ACMG interpretation guidelines in a research setting.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage pipeline development tasks independently under general guidance, troubleshoot technical software issues, and collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary research teams.
